description: Right-wing nationalist party. Largest party in the 25th Knesset (32 seats).
Center-left social-democratic party. 4 seats in 25th Knesset. Merged with Meretz to form The Democrats (הדמוקרטים) ahead of the 26th Knesset election.
Ultra-Orthodox Haredi political alliance of Agudat Yisrael and Degel HaTorah. 7 seats in 25th Knesset.
Centrist secular party focused on middle class and religious pluralism. 24 seats in 25th Knesset.
Right-wing party founded by Gideon Sa'ar in 2020. Merged into National Unity before the 2022 elections.
Center-right alliance led by Benny Gantz, formed from Blue and White and New Hope. 12 seats in 25th Knesset.
Ultra-Orthodox Sephardic religious party led by Arye Deri. 11 seats in 25th Knesset.
Far-right joint list of Smotrich (Religious Zionism), Ben-Gvir (Otzma Yehudit) and Noam. 14 seats in 25th Knesset.
Secular nationalist party led by Avigdor Lieberman, representing Russian-speaking community. 6 seats in 25th Knesset.
Islamist Arab party led by Mansour Abbas. 5 seats in 25th Knesset.
Joint list of Hadash (Arab-Jewish communist-democratic) and Ta'al (Arab nationalist). 5 seats in 25th Knesset.
Left-wing social-democratic party. Did not pass 3.25% threshold in 2022 (3.16%). Merged with Labor to form The Democrats (הדמוקרטים) ahead of the 26th Knesset election.

Left-Zionist party formed by merger of Labor (HaAvoda) and Meretz ahead of the 26th Knesset election. Led by Yair Golan (former IDF Deputy Chief of Staff). Combines social-democratic platform with Zionist security credentials.
